## The through-line (part 1)

*   Harm is contested, not measured
*   Regulation can and does work when it is not captured
*   Power and institutions set the rules
*   Markets are made, not natural

## The through-line (part 2)

*   People are social and fallible
*   Inequality is produced, not earned
*   Media manufacture the thinkable
*   Change comes from organized pressure

## One sentence each

*   Write one sentence naming a specific social-media or AI harm
*   Add the lesson that best explains it
*   Add one realistic response
*   No abstraction: name a product, a rule, and an action

## Collect the sentences

*   Go around the room and collect the sentences
*   Look for which lessons appear most and which are missing
*   This is the synthesis, not a new lecture

## Berlin's crooked timber

*   Berlin warned that monism, one supreme value, is the root of tyranny [@Berlin1991]
*   That is the trap the longtermist frame triggers
*   A single supreme value forecloses every other future
*   "Don't foreclose options" is the most defensible version of what we owe the future

## The pluralist close

*   Keep multiple values in play: care, fairness, liberty, accountability
*   The answers are not a single metric to optimize
*   They are a set of institutions to build and defend
*   Change is possible because it has happened

## Where to go next

*   Point to the reading list below
*   If running with colleagues, name a follow-up session or reading group
*   The harms are not mysterious and the responses are not untried
*   The question is whether we organize to use them
